hero.title: One Foundation result, several supporting views
payoff: Your completed Foundation can resolve to one archetype or a same-posture two-lens blend.
Strategic posture, normative orientation, and the closest modeled tradition help explain that result; Focus Areas and contextual records remain separate.
hero.boundary: Decision Patterns and evidence-coded public positions are reading aids. They never become your Foundation result.

sections.heading: How the labels fit together
sections.intro: The inventory uses a deliberate hierarchy so that supporting evidence never competes with the Foundation result.

sections.heading: Eight Foundation archetypes
sections.intro: Four explanatory lenses combine with two strategic postures. The rows summarize a continuous profile; they are not population types.

sections.heading: Variants and blends
sections.intro: Normative orientation changes how an archetype weighs order and justice. A blend keeps two lenses active under the same posture.

sections.heading: Four modeled traditions
sections.intro: The closest modeled tradition supports a Foundation reading; it is not a second Foundation result. Each tradition remains broader than the instrument can represent.

sections.heading: Seven Foundation dimensions
sections.intro: These dimensions preserve the tradeoffs beneath the headline label. A score describes a position within this model, not a percentile.

sections.heading: Decision Patterns
sections.intro: Decision Patterns are authored ways of approaching a choice. The directory supports comparison and does not calculate, match, or diagnose a user.

sections.heading: Thinkers and public positions
sections.intro: Published entries are dated, scoped interpretations built from cited public evidence. They describe a position within an evidence window and never assign a person or organization to an archetype.

sections.heading: Focus Areas and contextual records
sections.intro: Security and Technology are Focus Area questionnaires; AI Governance is a separate domain result; Perspective Runs are role-conditioned comparisons; Current Cases are time-bounded judgment exercises.

sections.heading: Coverage gaps and methods
sections.intro: Four modeled traditions do not exhaust International Relations. Important approaches remain under-modeled because the current dimensions and item coverage cannot represent them adequately.

hierarchy.label: Foundation result
hierarchy.description: One pure archetype or a legitimate same-posture blend supplies the headline Foundation reading.

hierarchy.label: Supporting interpretation
hierarchy.description: Strategic posture, normative orientation, and the closest modeled tradition explain parts of the result without replacing it.

hierarchy.label: Separate records
hierarchy.description: Focus Areas, AI Governance, Perspective Runs, and Current Case judgments remain scoped to their own questions.

scoringEvidence.body: Foundation scoring resolves the answers in a completed questionnaire. Historical comparisons and public positions use separate editorial evidence records; they do not feed back into the score.
scoringEvidence.linkLabel: Read the scoring and evidence method

lensBands.description: How leverage, position, and strategic timing shape the available choice.
How rules, enforcement, consultation, and restraint make cooperation durable.
How public meaning, legitimacy, and shared expectations shape what action can sustain.
How production, finance, capacity, and external dependence constrain practical choice.

normativeAliases.label: Order-first
normativeAliases.description: Starts by protecting coexistence, continuity, and limits on imposed agreement.

normativeAliases.label: Conditional
normativeAliases.description: Treats order and justice claims as conditional on the case, authority, and likely consequences.

normativeAliases.label: Justice-first
normativeAliases.description: Starts by asking what protection or obligation is owed beyond settled order.

blendExplanation: A blend appears only when two modeled lenses resolve close enough under one posture. It remains a family of nearby profiles; pair-specific interpretation is withheld until it receives editorial review.

dimensions.description: How much weight rivalry, uncertainty about intentions, and positional competition receive in an explanation.
How far rules, monitoring, and repeated interaction can make cooperation more durable.
How coalitions, regime type, capacity, and other domestic conditions shape foreign policy.
How legitimacy, recognition, identity, and social meaning shape interests and threats.
How production, finance, trade dependence, sanctions, and leverage shape room for action.
Whether the safer strategic instinct is to hold back or use an available advantage.
How sovereignty, settled order, wider protection, and moral obligation are weighed in tension.

contextBoundary: These records sit beside the Foundation. They do not rescore it.

contextRecords.title: Security
contextRecords.description: A Focus Area questionnaire about deterrence, escalation, alliances, and the use of force.

contextRecords.title: Technology
contextRecords.description: A Focus Area questionnaire about controls, capacity, openness, and strategic dependence.

contextRecords.title: AI Governance
contextRecords.description: A separate domain result about governance choices for advanced AI, kept outside the Foundation score.

contextRecords.title: Perspective Runs
contextRecords.description: Role-conditioned comparisons that show how a stable baseline travels under a defined vantage point.

contextRecords.title: Current Cases
contextRecords.description: Time-bounded judgment exercises with authored case readings and the user’s own recorded judgment.

coverage.canonNote: The Foundation draws mainly from traditions developed in Anglo-American and Western European International Relations. It does not adjust a score for nationality or culture, and it does not claim equivalent coverage across strategic traditions.
